Cubic sieves, a primitive-ratio cut and a 20/3720/37 bound for the a⁢b⁢cabc exceptional set

Ruiyi Zhang Independent Researcher, Columbia, Maryland, USA
Abstract.

We prove N1⁢(X)≪εX20/37+εN_{1}(X)\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{20/37+\varepsilon}, where Nλ⁢(X)N_{\lambda}(X) counts the a⁢b⁢cabc triples of exponent λ\lambda in [1,X]3[1,X]^{3}. The previous full bound was X13/20+εX^{13/20+\varepsilon}. We use the anatomic reduction of Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teräväinen. Five families add new rows. The first two are an archimedean cover and a row from Heath-Brown’s uniform bound for diagonal cubic curves. Spacing gives 3030 two-arm clauses. Cubic characters and a fourth moment of Dirichlet LL-functions give the cubic-sieve rows. Cochrane and Shi’s fourth moment gives the moment rows. An exact Farkas certificate with 394 633394\,633 leaves gives exponent 20/3720/37 for the box count. On each leaf the multipliers of all rows except nonnegativity sum to at most 586/201586/201. Exact rows are included in this sum. This pays for the losses at λ=1\lambda=1.

Key words and phrases:
abc conjecture, exceptional set, radical, anatomy of integers, power sieve, character sums, Farey fractions, linear programming certificate
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:
Primary 11D75; Secondary 11N25, 11N36, 11L40, 11D25, 11Y16

1. Introduction

For this paper ℕ={1,2,…}\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,\ldots\}. For n≠0n\neq 0 put rad⁡(n)=∏p∣np\operatorname{rad}(n)=\prod_{p\mid n}p, and write ω⁢(n)=#⁢{p:p∣n}\omega(n)=\#\{p:p\mid n\}, with ω⁢(1)=0\omega(1)=0. Following [2], call (a,b,c)∈ℕ3(a,b,c)\in\mathbb{N}^{3} with gcd⁡(a,b,c)=1\gcd(a,b,c)=1 an a⁢b⁢cabc triple of exponent λ\lambda if

(1.1) a+b=c,rad⁡(a⁢b⁢c)<cλ.a+b=c,\qquad\operatorname{rad}(abc)<c^{\lambda}.

Let Nλ⁢(X)N_{\lambda}(X) count these triples in [1,X]3[1,X]^{3}. The a⁢b⁢cabc conjecture of Masser and Oesterlé implies that Nλ⁢(X)=Oλ⁢(1)N_{\lambda}(X)=O_{\lambda}(1) for λ<1\lambda<1, so λ=1\lambda=1 is the endpoint of interest.

The bound Nλ⁢(X)≪εX2⁢λ/3+εN_{\lambda}(X)\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{2\lambda/3+\varepsilon} is classical [2, Proposition 1.1]; it comes from de Bruijn’s count [5] of integers with restricted radical. For λ≥2\lambda\geq 2, Kane’s result [10] gives Nλ⁢(X)≪εXλ−1+εN_{\lambda}(X)\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{\lambda-1+\varepsilon} [2, Section 1]. On 2≤λ≤32\leq\lambda\leq 3 it matches Nλ⁢(X)≫Xλ−1−εN_{\lambda}(X)\gg X^{\lambda-1-\varepsilon}. Granville’s unpublished work gives the lower bound for 1<λ≤31<\lambda\leq 3, as reported in [2, Section 1]. The question is Mazur’s. It can hold only for λ≤3\lambda\leq 3, since Nλ⁢(X)≤#⁢{(a,b,c)∈[1,X]3:a+b=c}=O⁢(X2)N_{\lambda}(X)\leq\#\{(a,b,c)\in[1,X]^{3}:a+b=c\}=O(X^{2}). Browning, Lichtman and Teräväinen [3, Theorem 1.2] gave the first power saving below 2⁢λ/32\lambda/3, for 0.99<λ<1.0010.99<\lambda<1.001. Bernert [1, Theorem 1] proved

(1.2) Nλ⁢(X)≪εX(23⁢λ+3)/40+ε(0<λ<2),N_{\lambda}(X)\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{(23\lambda+3)/40+\varepsilon}\qquad(0<% \lambda<2),

so N1⁢(X)≪εX13/20+εN_{1}(X)\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{13/20+\varepsilon}. In the merged paper, [2, Theorem 1.2] states (1.2) for 0<λ≤20<\lambda\leq 2. Its Theorem 1.3 gives 0.60.6 for 0<λ<10<\lambda<1, with a constant depending on λ\lambda. At λ=1\lambda=1: a remark at the end of [1, Section 4] sketches 8/13=0.6153⁢…8/13=0.6153\ldots; Li [11] obtains 56/85=0.6588⁢…56/85=0.6588\ldots from the method of [3], its limit without further optimisation by his account.

Theorem 1.

N1⁢(X)≪εX20/37+εN_{1}(X)\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{20/37+\varepsilon}, where 20/37=0.5405⁢…20/37=0.5405\ldots

Since Nμ≤N1N_{\mu}\leq N_{1} for μ≤1\mu\leq 1, Theorem 1 also improves [2, Theorem 1.3] on 0<μ<10<\mu<1, with a constant independent of μ\mu. Among the estimates cited here, the resulting exponent is min⁡{2⁢μ/3,20/37}\min\{2\mu/3,20/37\} for 0<μ≤10<\mu\leq 1. Thus the new exponent is best known for 30/37<μ≤130/37<\mu\leq 1; it ties the classical exponent at μ=30/37\mu=30/37. Its crossing with the Bernert exponent alone is μ=689/851\mu=689/851.

Section 2 recalls the anatomic reduction of [3, 1, 2]. Fix ε0>0\varepsilon_{0}>0 and d=d⁢(ε0)d=d(\varepsilon_{0}). Every triple lies in a box. In a box, each side is a fixed coefficient times ∏i≤d𝔰ii\prod_{i\leq d}\mathfrak{s}_{i}^{\,i}. The roots 𝔰i\mathfrak{s}_{i} have fixed dyadic sizes. The three side values are pairwise coprime. Section 2 works at a generic scale XX and exponent λ\lambda; Lemma 12.2 applies it at the scale YY of (2.1), with λ:=μ\lambda:=\mu and base-YY logarithms. The quantity VsV_{s} is the weighted exponent of the root product, excluding its fixed coefficient, as defined in Section 6; hd=d⁢(d+1)/2h_{d}=d(d+1)/2. The quantity ρ\rho is the largest finite right-hand-side shift in Lemma 12.2. The bound on ρ\rho holds for Y≥Y0⁢(ε0,d)Y\geq Y_{0}(\varepsilon_{0},d). Smaller YY contribute Oε0,d⁢(1)O_{\varepsilon_{0},d}(1), and μ≤0\mu\leq 0 contributes nothing (Section 13).

N1⁢(X)≪(log⁡X)2⁢maxY≤X,μ≤1⁡Nμ∗⁢(Y),Nμ∗⁢(Y)≪Yε0⁢max⁡ℬd,D≤2037+ΛU⁢ρ,ΛU=586201,ρ≤19⁢ε0,\begin{gathered}N_{1}(X)\ll(\log X)^{2}\max_{Y\leq X,\ \mu\leq 1}N^{*}_{\mu}(Y% ),\qquad N^{*}_{\mu}(Y)\ll Y^{\varepsilon_{0}}\max\mathcal{B}_{d},\\ D\leq\frac{20}{37}+\Lambda_{U}\rho,\qquad\Lambda_{U}=\frac{586}{201},\qquad% \rho\leq 19\varepsilon_{0},\end{gathered}

from (2.1), (2.3), Theorem 2 with Lemma 12.1, and Lemma 12.2. Since 19⁢ΛU+1=1133520119\Lambda_{U}+1=\frac{11335}{201}, choosing ε0\varepsilon_{0} with 11335201⁢ε0<ε/2\frac{11335}{201}\,\varepsilon_{0}<\varepsilon/2 proves Theorem 1.

The inequalities for DD are linear in 2828 exponents. They are the root and tail coordinates of the three sides, DD, and three auxiliary Fourier variables. BBLT’s Theorem 1.3 gives the 3/53/5 bound. gcd⁡(u,v)=1,u≡ξ⁢v(modM),0<u≤Ucut,0<v≤Vcut.\gcd(u,v)=1,\qquad u\equiv\xi v\pmod{M},\qquad 0<u\leq U_{\rm cut},\quad 0<v% \leq V_{\rm cut}.

The paper adds five further families.

In the limiting coordinates, Va,Vb≤VcV_{a},V_{b}\leq V_{c}, and Vc≤VaV_{c}\leq V_{a} or Vc≤VbV_{c}\leq V_{b}. At finite scale, Va,Vb≤Vc+ε0/2V_{a},V_{b}\leq V_{c}+\varepsilon_{0}/2, and one of Vc≤Va+3⁢ε0/2+logY⁡21+hdV_{c}\leq V_{a}+3\varepsilon_{0}/2+\log_{Y}2^{1+h_{d}} or Vc≤Vb+3⁢ε0/2+logY⁡21+hdV_{c}\leq V_{b}+3\varepsilon_{0}/2+\log_{Y}2^{1+h_{d}} holds.

    Cubic (Section 7). Fix all roots but the three cube roots. Heath-Brown’s bound [8, Theorem 1.3] for primitive points on α⁢x3+β⁢y3=γ⁢z3\alpha x^{3}+\beta y^{3}=\gamma z^{3}, uniform in the coefficients, gives D≤L−p3D\leq L-p_{3}. Here LL and pip_{i} are as in Section 2.

    Moments (Section 10). Expand the congruence of the cut modulo MM by characters. The fourth moment of Cochrane and Shi [4, Theorem 1] bounds the nonprincipal part: 188 976188\,976 clauses.

Section 11 proves D≤20/37D\leq 20/37 from these rows. The certificate is a finite trie. Each internal node splits on one clause, one child per arm. Each leaf carries nonnegative rational Farkas multipliers. There are 394 633394\,633 leaves, depth 4949, and no infeasible leaf. On a leaf the multipliers of all rows except nonnegativity sum to at most ΛU=586/201\Lambda_{U}=586/201, whence the term ΛU⁢ρ\Lambda_{U}\rho. This includes exact rows. A point of the installed system attains 20/3720/37; the qualification on this optimum appears in Section 11.2.

Section 12 treats μ=1\mu=1. In the proof of Theorem 1, the dyadic reduction only requires 0<μ≤10<\mu\leq 1. At this endpoint the row L≤1L\leq 1 of [2] is unavailable: the proof of [2, Theorem 1.3] uses ε0≤(1−μ)/3\varepsilon_{0}\leq(1-\mu)/3. We use L≤1+3⁢ε0/4L\leq 1+3\varepsilon_{0}/4 instead. The LL-native Fourier and geometry rows cost 18⁢ε018\varepsilon_{0} and 6⁢ε06\varepsilon_{0}. After the choice of Y0Y_{0} in Lemma 12.2, every new row costs at most 2⁢ε02\varepsilon_{0}. Hence ρ=18⁢ε0+oε0,d⁢(1)\rho=18\varepsilon_{0}+o_{\varepsilon_{0},d}(1) and ΛU⁢ρ=351667⁢ε0+oε0,d⁢(1)\Lambda_{U}\rho=\frac{3516}{67}\,\varepsilon_{0}+o_{\varepsilon_{0},d}(1).

The proof in [2] does not use the determinant method; [3] used it together with Thue equations. Lemma 4.1 is an elementary lattice-point count of the kind used in [2, Proposition 4.1]. The cut applies it to two sides at once, with modulus MM built from roots on the third side.

Imported statements are cited where used. Citations of [2] refer to arXiv:2410.12234v2 (to appear in C. R. Math.); each imported statement was checked against it. The dyadic reduction (2.1) is only stated in [2, Section 2]; Section 2 proves it. Appendix A reproves the estimates of [2, Propositions 2.3, 3.1 and 4.1] for our boxes. They use the divisor bound, the count of solutions of xj−yj=mx^{j}-y^{j}=m (Lemma A.1) and the lattice-point bound [7, Lemma 3] (Theorem C). The new rows use the cubic bound [8, Theorem 1.3] and the fourth moments [6, Lemma 4] and [4, Theorem 1]. The cubic-sieve character expansion (Section 9) also uses the classical Jacobi-sum bound [9]. No conjecture is assumed. Theorem 2 has multiplier bound ΛU\Lambda_{U}. It is computer-assisted and uses a certificate checked by the standard-library programs in Appendix C. The analytic reductions and row families are proved in the text.

The three side values of a box are pairwise coprime. Hence every factor of one side is a unit modulo every factor of another side.

Appendix C Computer checks

The paper comes with external files. They are the certificate report of Theorem 2 and the checking programs of Table C.2. The rows, witness (11.7), and verification procedures are specified in the text. All arithmetic is exact. No checking program imports a numerical package or an LP solver.

C.1. The report

The file final-report.raw.json.xz decompresses to the report. normalize_completed_report.py recomputes its derived trie statistics; on this report its output equals its input byte for byte. The report is one JSON object with fields target ("20/37"), system, search_flags, complete, stats, certificates, survivors, open_stack and elapsed_s. The lists survivors and open_stack are empty. Each certificate has exactly four fields.

  • •

    kind: always "upper".

  • •

    path: the list of arm labels from the root to the leaf.

  • •

    terms: a list of [row-label,"p/q"], multipliers positive.

  • •

    rhs: the value ∑iηi⁢bi\sum_{i}\eta_{i}b_{i}.

The paths form the trie of Theorem 2. A label names one row or arm of 𝒮\mathcal{S} (Table C.1). The verifier rebuilds each row from its label and reads no stored coefficient vector. The metadata string system also contains the label DET. It names a row family outside 𝒮\mathcal{S}. The verifier builds no row from it, and no path or multiplier in this certificate uses such a row.

program what it checks
verify_tree_report_clean.py Standard library only. Strict JSON, duplicate keys rejected; target, system string and flags. At each leaf: every label well formed and in 𝒮\mathcal{S}; every term a linear row, a row −xk≤0-x_{k}\leq 0, or an arm on the path; (11.4) exactly, that is ∑iηi⁢gi=eD\sum_{i}\eta_{i}g_{i}=e_{D} and ∑iηi⁢bi≤20/37\sum_{i}\eta_{i}b_{i}\leq 20/37; the declared rhs. The trie: paths distinct and prefix-free; the children of each internal node are exactly the arms of one clause, (6.5) included at any depth. It recomputes Tables 11.2 and 11.3 and ΛU\Lambda_{U}. It rejects 4646 corrupted reports, among them a missing arm, a missing (6.5) arm, a tampered multiplier, a row outside its path, a forbidden POW3⁢(a)\mathrm{POW3}(a) descriptor and a prefix leaf.
verify_tree_report.py a second replay of (11.4) and of the node counts
verify_witness_clean.py x∗x^{*} against every clause of 𝒮\mathcal{S} (Table 11.4); it rejects 1919 corrupted constructors
audit_clause_compiler.py, compiler_differential_used.py every row used by the certificate, and every POW3\mathrm{POW3} and grouped descriptor, rebuilt by the search program’s compiler and compared with the verifier’s row

The driver runs these programs and writes their output:

run_verification.sh ⟶\longrightarrow FROZEN_VERIFICATION.stdout.

Soundness uses the displayed row definitions and the label map in Table C.1. It also uses the exact Farkas identities at every leaf and the admissibility and trie checks of the first program. The compiler differential also compares the verifier’s row builder with the search compiler. The coefficient formulas and derivations in Sections 2–B identify those rows with the system 𝒮\mathcal{S}.

Table C.1 gives the labels. Here s∈{a,b,c}s\in\{a,b,c\}; σ\sigma is the modulus or powered side; (y,z)(y,z) is as in Section 5. A set T⊆{1,…,6,tail}T\subseteq\{1,\dots,6,\mathrm{tail}\} is written as the integer ∑t∈T2t−1\sum_{t\in T}2^{t-1}, with the tail counted as t=7t=7. Free sets Ry,RzR_{y},R_{z} are written likewise, in [1,63][1,63] or 0. Slots are written a1, …, c6.
